 Advertisement USS Harry S. Truman sailors visit president’s library in Independence
 Advertisement Updated: 10:36 PM CST Nov 11, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jamie Weiss KMBC 9 News Anchor USS Harry S. Truman sailors visit president’s library in Independence
 Updated: 10:36 PM CST Nov 11, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jamie Weiss KMBC 9 News Anchor Sailors from the USS Harry Truman visited Independence, Missouri, to connect with the legacy of President Harry Truman at his presidential library. 
 "I feel like it's like some kind of sign," said LS3 Mikhaya Evans. 
 Advertisement Eden Paulos, Sailor of the Year, expressed her enthusiasm for the visit. 
 "I was like, I want to go and I want to see what Missouri's all about. And, President Truman has so much history, and this town is just rich in history. And so it's just an awesome experience just to be here," Paulos said. 
 The sailors toured Truman's presidential library. 
 "My stepdad, he was in the Navy, and he was talking about how I might go to the USS Harry Truman, and it was just a big ol coincidence that it happened. It's an honor. It's an honor serving my hometown's president, out to sea every day," said Austin Setton. 
 Others said their visit there helped provide an understanding of the former president's life. 
 "Since I'm on the ship, I feel like it'll be a different perspective. Seeing these things and learning it and being able to take it in a lot more," Evans said. 
 "It's just a big honor, you know, growing up with Harry Truman around me and then going to work every day with President Truman, there," Setton said said. 
 Evans shared her aspirations for the future. 
 "I hope that my legacy is to motivate people to also be a part of something bigger," she said.
